title: Drift-aware evaluation matrix and judge uncertainty protocol
creator: Ayesha Malik
description:
Problem: We observe inconsistent regression signals when small model/config changes are rolled out: scoped cohorts show degradation while global metrics remain stable, and LLM-as-judge outputs have unstable confidence distributions across cohorts. Current rubric weights and single-judge scores mask these localized regressions, causing late rollbacks or noisy alerts.

Goal: Define and implement a drift-aware evaluation matrix and a judge-uncertainty protocol that: (1) adapts rubric weights by cohort drift signals, (2) quantifies judge-level uncertainty and propagates it to rollout gating, and (3) provides per-change attributions so Product/Eng can act on root causes rather than noisy signals. The output should integrate with the rollout controller to block/flag canaries that exceed uncertainty-informed thresholds.

Scope:
- Define cohorting strategy (static user segments + dynamic traffic clusters) and drift detection heuristics.
- Design a weighting scheme that adjusts rubric component importance when cohorts drift from historical baselines.
- Establish an LLM-judge ensemble protocol that reports score + calibrated uncertainty and a method to combine judges (hierarchical ensembling).
- Implement attribution signals (rubric component deltas, prompt-config diffs, model-variant diffs) surfaced in the Console and eval dashboards.
- Integration points: eval pipeline (batch and streaming), rollout gating hooks, alerting rules in Console, and automated QA playbooks.

Out of scope for this ticket: full infra rework for streaming judge aggregation (will be a follow-up ENG ticket), real-time active learning for judges (future phase).
acceptance_criteria: Cohorting spec document published (static + dynamic cluster definitions) with examples and dataset queries
Rubric-weight adaptation algorithm specified with pseudocode and unit tests for simulated drift scenarios
LLM-judge ensemble protocol defined: how many judges, pooling rules, and uncertainty metrics (e.g., predictive entropy + calibration curve)
End-to-end eval pipeline produces per-change report with: global score, cohort scores, judge-uncertainty band, and component-level attribution
Console shows a new "Drift & Uncertainty" section for rollout artifacts and flags canary rollouts when uncertainty-adjusted delta > threshold
Runbook for SRE/SEV responses for false positives/negatives linked from the ticket
